summary: Tenant routing lockout after conditional canary pause removes version anchor for some sessions
description:
Issue summary: During a conditional canary pause (weight set to 0 while prewarm probes finished) some tenant sessions lost their model version anchor and were routed to the degraded fallback variant. Impact: BrightWrite reported repeated degraded-model responses and a billing increase from retrying requests. Estimated affected user fraction: ~2% of active sessions for BrightWrite in us-west during the 09:30-10:15 UTC window. Environment: Production, dedicated pool in us-west, ingress through edge-proxy cluster ep-12, orchestrator version 3.7.2. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a gradual promote: set canary weight 10->5->0 while keeping prewarm probes enabled. 2) Have long-lived chat sessions from the tenant with session-affinity cookies. 3) Trigger a rolling prewarm pause by toggling the conditional-probe flag. 4) Observe routing decision logs and model anchor state for session IDs.
Observed logs and telemetry:
- Edge-proxy trace ep-12 shows affinity cookie present but route decision dropped model_anchor header for ~1 in 50 requests.
- Orchestrator recorded a transient lockout for cohort commit during the pause: "commit-window-skip: tenant=brightwrite, cohort=246, reason=conditional-canary-pause".
- Serving-runtime returned 503 for some prewarm probes which triggered fallback activation.
- Console traces show fallback routing spike aligned to the pause window and higher token costs due to retries.
Hypothesis: When the orchestrator enters the paused prewarm state, an internal commit check bail-out path clears per-session anchor metadata for cohorts undergoing conditional prewarm. This leaves edge decision logic without an explicit pinned version, and because the health probe observed degraded responses, requests were routed to the fallback variant.
Likely contributing factors: race between prewarm probe state transitions and edge route memoization TTL, and an edge header sanitizer that canonicalizes anchor headers and may drop them when the canary weight reaches zero.
Temporary workaround provided to customer: 1) Re-enable canary weight to 5% to reestablish prewarm continuity while we investigate. 2) If immediate stability required, set an explicit model_version override on the tenant route to force anchoring until patch deployed. Workarounds observed to reduce impact within 3 minutes of application.
Next steps / action items:
- SRE to reproduce locally with a dedicated small-scale canary and long-lived sessions (assigned: Marco).
- Engineering (orchestrator) to add an audit log when commit-path bail-outs clear session anchors and to avoid clearing anchors until cohort commit finalizes (assigned: Priya Desai).
- Edge team to review header sanitizer path for anchor header drop during weight=0 transitions (assigned: Linh Tran).
- Add a canary-runbook step to ensure prewarm probe stabilization for 2 minutes before any weight=0 action.
- Customer success: monitor BrightWrite for next 24 hours and confirm stability after mitigation.
Owner notes: we have a reproduction run scheduled in staging 2026-03-14T14:00Z. Priority is high due to customer impact and cost exposure. This ticket captures the customer-facing incident; a follow-up internal postmortem will be created if root cause confirmed.
